analysis.title: Nasdaq Futures: Falling Out of Favor
key_insights: Nasdaq's funding premium over the S&P reversed from roughly a 1-year max over the past 6 sessions, which the note reads as potential bearish flow via leveraged products. The 3-month Nasdaq vs S&P funding differential fell from a 99% rank on Nov 6 to 64% by the Nov 16 close.
Commitment of Traders data for Nov 3-10 shows Non-Dealer futures liquidation. Non-Dealers net sold $6.9bn, made up of $8.1bn of long unwinds partly offset by $1.2bn of short covering.
The 'Other' category led the selling with a multiyear record in total selling of $9bn.

Longs kept unwinding after Nov 10, then fears of chip export curbs spurred sizeable shorts. Aggregate futures open interest lost about $2bn per session over Nov 10-13 as the Jensen Huang saga unfolded.
On Nov 16 the US Commerce Department's crackdown on chip shipments to China sent Nasdaq down 2.7%. Futures open interest rose $8.2bn, the 5th largest 1-day gain in 2026 excluding roll periods.
Tactically there is scope for a relief rally. In early trading on Nov 17, Nasdaq futures reached intraday highs of +0.8%, testing the resolve of the new shorts.
The potential for larger selling remains. The notional rank of Nasdaq Non-Dealer net positioning on Nov 10 was 99% on a 2-year lookback.

sector_views.rationale: Chip export curbs drove new shorts in Nasdaq futures. A short-term relief rally is possible, but the note flags the risk of larger selling.

risk_factors: Larger selling risk given Non-Dealer net positioning at a 99% notional rank (2-year lookback) on Nov 10.
Further US chip export restrictions on China.
Leveraged-product bearish flow, as signaled by the reversal in the funding premium.
